title: Distribution of squid and fish in the pelagic zone of the Cosmonaut Sea and Prydz Bay region during the BROKE-West campaign - data
description: Fish data collected by a RMT net. Samples were collected during the BROKE-west cruise of RV ‘‘Aurora Australis’’ (05/06 V3) in 20 the CCAMLR statistical subarea 58.4.2, between January 2 and March 17, 2006. The sampling grid consisted of eleven longitudinal transects between 30° and 80° E and 58°S south to the Antarctic coastline. Fish were caught using Rectangular Midwater Trawl nets (RMT 8 + 1), consisting of a RMT 1 mounted above a RMT 8 with a mouth area of 1 and 8 m² and a cod end mesh size of 0.33 and 0.85 mm, respectively. Two types of methods were used: target trawls and routine trawls. Target trawls were not pre-planned and were aimed at acoustically detected aggregations. The net was lowered to the depth of the aggregation, and opened and closed remotely. Routine hauls consisted of a standard double oblique tow from the surface down to 200 5 m and back again to the surface. Towing speed was approximately 2.5 knots (4.5 km h-1).

fields.rdfs:comment: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geographic coordinates given in dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude are based.

fields.name: footprintSRS

fields.description: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geometry given in dwc:footprintWKT is based.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use the EPSG code of the SRS, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the geodetic datum, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the ellipsoid, if known. If none of these is known, use the value `not recorded`. It is also permitted to provide the SRS in Well-Known-Text, especially if no EPSG code provides the necessary values for the attributes of the SRS. Do not use this term to describe the SRS of the dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude, nor of any verbatim coordinates - use the dwc:geodeticDatum and dwc:verbatimSRS instead. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `EPSG:4326`; `GEOGCS["GCS_WGS_1984", DATUM["D_WGS_1984", SPHEROID["WGS_1984",6378137,298.257223563]], PRIMEM["Greenwich",0], UNIT["Degree",0.0174532925199433]]` (WKT for the standard WGS84 Spatial Reference System EPSG:4326); `not recorded`
fields.rdfs:comment: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geometry given in dwc:footprintWKT is based.

fields.name: scientificName

fields.description: A scientific name string, not including authorship, date or identification qualifiers.
fields.comments: When applied to an Organism or Occurrence, this term should be used to represent the scientific name that was applied to the associated Organism in accordance with the Taxon to which it was or is currently identified. For example, names of hybrids for algae, fungi and plants should follow the rules of the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Schenzhen Code Articles H.1, H.2 and H.3). Thus, use the multiplication sign `×` (Unicode `U+00D7`, HTML `×`) to identify a hybrid, not `x` or `X`, if possible.

This property optionally allows the presentation of detailed information and will in most cases be shown together with the resource title. If both a description and a caption are present in the metadata, a description is typically displayed instead of the resource, whereas a caption is displayed together with the resource. The description should aim to be a good proxy for the underlying media resource in cases where only text can be shown, whereas the caption may only make sense when shown together with the media. fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of the globally unique identifiers for the funding organizations or agencies that supported the project.

fields.name: fundingAttributionID
fields.title: Funding Attribution ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent that financially supported a project.
fields.comments: Provide a unique identifier for the funding body, such as an identifier used in governmental or international databases. If no official identifier exists, use a persistent and unique identifier within your organization or dataset. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent that financially supported a project.

fields.name: references
fields.title: References
fields.description: A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource.
fields.comments: This property is intended to be used with non-literal values. This property is an inverse property of Is Referenced By.
fields.rdfs:comment: A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource.

fields.name: projectID
fields.title: Project ID
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of identifiers for projects that contributed to a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: A projectID may be shared in multiple distinct datasets. The nature of the association can be described in the metadata project description element. This term should be used to provide a globally unique identifier (GUID) for a project, if available. This could be a DOI, URI, or any other persistent identifier that ensures a project can be uniquely distinguished from others. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of identifiers for projects that contributed to a dwc:Event.

fields.name: projectTitle
fields.title: Project Title
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of titles or names for projects that contributed to a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Use this term to provide the official name or title of a project as it is commonly known and cited. Avoid abbreviations unless they are widely understood. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `Arctic Deep`; `Scalidophora i Noreg`; `The Nansen Legacy`; `Underwater Oases of the Mar del Plata Canyon: Talud Continental IV`
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of titles or names for projects that contributed to a dwc:Event.

fields.name: surveyID
fields.title: Survey ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Survey.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: eventID
fields.title: Event ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: siteCount
fields.title: Site Count
fields.description: Total number of individual sites surveyed during a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy.
fields.rdfs:comment: Total number of individual sites surveyed during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: siteNestingDescription
fields.title: Site Nesting Description
fields.description: Textual description of a hierarchical sampling design.
fields.comments: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy.
fields.rdfs:comment: Textual description of the hierarchical sampling design.

fields.name: verbatimSiteDescriptions
fields.title: Verbatim Site Descriptions
fields.description: Original textual description of site(s).
fields.comments: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `Wet flatwoods | Wet depression surrounded by mesic longleaf pine flatwoods | Ground cover of thick Andropogon spp., Sporobolus floridanus, Vaccinium spp, Rhynchospora spp., Centella erecta, Panicum rigidulum.`
fields.rdfs:comment: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space ( | ).

fields.name: verbatimSiteNames
fields.title: Verbatim Site Names
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of original site names.
fields.comments: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `East Coastal Fringe | St. Marks Wildlife Management Area`; `S1 | S2 | C1 | C2 | R14 | R22 | W1`
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of original site names.

fields.name: isAbsenceReported
fields.title: Is Absence Reported
fields.description: Taxonomic absences were reported.
fields.comments: Absences can be reported at any taxonomic level.
fields.rdfs:comment: Taxonomic absences were reported.

fields.name: areNonTargetTaxaFullyReported
fields.title: Are Non Target Taxa Fully Reported
fields.description: Every dwc:Organism that was outside of the target taxonomic scope (the combination of eco:targetTaxonomicScope and eco:excludedTaxonomicScope) and detected during a dwc:Event, and that was detectable using the given protocol (given in eco:protocolDescriptions and dwc:samplingProtocol), was reported.
fields.comments: This term is meant to inform a user of the data whether there were non-target taxa that were detected, but left unreported. This term is only relevant if a dwc:Event used restricted search or open search methods and if a target taxonomic scope is declared. Taxonomic scope is based on the combination of eco:targetTaxonomicScope and eco:excludedTaxonomicScope. Within dwc:Events that used either a restricted search or an open search method and declared a taxonomic scope, if all dwc:Organisms that are not included within the target taxonomic scope and that were detected during a dwc:Event were reported, the value of this term should be 'true', otherwise the value of this term should be ‘false'.
fields.rdfs:comment: Every dwc:Organism that was outside of the target taxonomic scope (the combination of eco:targetTaxonomicScope and eco:excludedTaxonomicScope) and detected during the dwc:Event, and that was detectable using the given protocol (given in eco:protocolDescriptions and dwc:samplingProtocol), was reported.

fields.name: compilationTypes
fields.title: Compilation Types
fields.description: A statement specifying whether data reported are derived from sampling events, ancillary data compiled from other sources, or a combination of both.
fields.comments: This term is only relevant if a dwc:Event is an inventory. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A statement specifying whether data reported are derived from sampling events, ancillary data compiled from other sources, or a combination of both.

fields.name: inventoryTypes
fields.title: Inventory Types
fields.description: The types of search processes used to conduct the inventory.
fields.comments: This term is only relevant if a dwc:Event represents an inventory. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: The types of search processes used to conduct the inventory.

fields.name: protocolNames
fields.title: Protocol Names
fields.description: Categorical descriptive names for the dwc:Protocols used during a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary and separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: Categorical descriptive names for the methods used during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: protocolReferences
fields.title: Protocol References
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of dcterms:BibliographicResources used in a dwc:Protocol.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `Penguins from space: faecal stains reveal the location of emperor penguin colonies, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1466-8238.2009.00467.x`
fields.rdfs:comment: The references to the methods used during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: isLeastSpecificTargetCategoryQuantityInclusive
fields.title: Is Least Specific Target Category Quantity Inclusive
fields.description: The total detected quantity for a dwc:Taxon (including subcategories thereof) in a dwc:Event is given explicitly in a single record (dwc:organismQuantity value) for that dwc:Taxon.
fields.comments: Recommended values are 'true' and 'false'. This term is only relevant if dwc:organismQuantity is a number. For a detailed explanation, see http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/doc/inclusive/.
fields.rdfs:comment: The total detected quantity for a dwc:Taxon (including subcategories thereof) in a dwc:Event is given explicitly in a single record (dwc:organismQuantity value) for that dwc:Taxon.

fields.name: sampleSizeValue
fields.title: Sample Size Value
fields.description: A numeric value for a measurement of the size (time duration, length, area, or volume) of a sample in a sampling dwc:Event.
fields.comments: A dwc:sampleSizeValue must have a corresponding dwc:sampleSizeUnit.
fields.rdfs:comment: A numeric value for a measurement of the size (time duration, length, area, or volume) of a sample in a sampling dwc:Event.

fields.name: sampleSizeUnit
fields.title: Sample Size Unit
fields.description: The unit of measurement of the size (time duration, length, area, or volume) of a sample in a sampling dwc:Event.
fields.comments: A dwc:sampleSizeUnit must have a corresponding dwc:sampleSizeValue, e.g., `5` for dwc:sampleSizeValue with `m` for dwc:sampleSizeUnit. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: The unit of measurement of the size (time duration, length, area, or volume) of a sample in a sampling dwc:Event.

fields.name: samplingPerformedBy
fields.title: Sampling Performed By
fields.description: A dcterms:Agent responsible for sampling.
fields.comments: The sampling dwc:Event could be at any level of hierarchy. In the case of a higher level (parent) dwc:Event, include all the organizations or people involved in the child dwc:Events that contributed to the parent dwc:Event. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `North American Butterfly Association`; `KK Wall`; `JJ Green`; `LL Pink and FF Grey | Aspen Center for Environmental Studies`
fields.rdfs:comment: A person, group, or organization responsible for recording the dwc:Event.

fields.name: samplingPerformedByID
fields.title: Sampling Performed By ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent responsible for sampling.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to provide a single identifier that disambiguates the details of the sampling dcterms:Agent. If a list is used, the order of the identifiers on the list should not be assumed to convey any semantics. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).

fields.name: isSamplingEffortReported
fields.title: Is Sampling Effort Reported
fields.description: The sampling effort associated with a dwc:Event was reported.
fields.comments: Typically values of effort would be captured under the terms eco:samplingEffortValue and eco:samplingEffortUnit.
fields.rdfs:comment: The sampling effort associated with the dwc:Event was reported.

fields.name: samplingEffortProtocol
fields.title: Sampling Effort Protocol
fields.description: A description of or reference to a Protocol used to determine a eco:samplingEffortValue.
fields.comments: This description should be associated with the values reported in eco:samplingEffortValue and eco:samplingEffortUnit. This is a specialization of eco:protocolDescriptions focused on effort, distinct from the survey method. The effort relates to the intensity of sampling and therefore can assist in interpreting estimates of completeness. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `40 box traps deployed at even spacings along 4 parallel 100m transects placed 50m apart and visited at 6 hourly intervals over a 48 hour period`; `2 people occupying a bird hide for a period of 8 hours and undertaking a 30 minute count of species within the 150 degree field of view every 2 hours`; `A single baited camera trap station with motion sensor trigger, deployed for a period of 10 days and configured for detecting large fauna moving through a known traffic way`
fields.rdfs:comment: A description of or reference (publication or URL) to the methods used to determine the sampling effort.

fields.name: samplingEffortValue
fields.title: Sampling Effort Value
fields.description: The numeric value for the sampling effort expended during a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: This term is meant to capture the total sampling effort value. To express details of how the effort was determined use eco:samplingEffortProtocol. For compilations it is recommend not to infer effort. An eco:samplingEffortValue must have a corresponding eco:samplingEffortUnit.
fields.rdfs:comment: The numeric value for the sampling effort expended during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: samplingEffortUnit
fields.title: Sampling Effort Unit
fields.description: Units associated with a value in eco:samplingEffortValue.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: The units associated with the eco:samplingEffortValue.

fields.name: surveyTargetID
fields.title: Survey Target ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:SurveyTarget.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier. Note: values of this term are not meant to be unique within a dwc:SurveyTarget. A full dwc:SurveyTarget is composed of all records that share the same dwc:surveyTargetID.

fields.name: surveyID
fields.title: Survey ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Survey.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: surveyTargetType
fields.title: Survey Target Type
fields.description: A scope a dwc:SurveyTarget describes.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: surveyTargetTypeIRI
fields.title: Survey Target Type IRI
fields.description: An IRI of a controlled vocabulary value for a type of target.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an IRI for a term in a controlled vocabulary.
fields.rdfs:comment: The nature or genre of the resource.

fields.name: surveyTargetValue
fields.title: Survey Target Value
fields.description: A value of a characteristic to include or exclude in a dwc:SurveyTarget for a given dwc:surveyTargetType.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: surveyTargetValueIRI
fields.title: Survey Target Value IRI
fields.description: An IRI of a controlled vocabulary value for a target value.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an IRI for a term in a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: surveyTargetUnit
fields.title: Survey Target Unit
fields.description: Unit associated with a value in dwc:surveyTargetValue.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: surveyTargetUnitIRI
fields.title: Survey Target Unit IRI
fields.description: An IRI of a controlled vocabulary value for a target unit.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an IRI for a term in a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: includeOrExclude
fields.title: Include Or Exclude
fields.description: Whether the combination of dwc:surveyTargetType and dwc:surveyTargetValue is included or excluded in a dwc:SurveyTarget.
fields.comments: Combinations of dwc:SurveyTarget records of inclusions and exclusions can define complex scopes such as all flying adult Aves except Passeriformes. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary consisting of 'include' and 'exclude' only.

fields.name: isSurveyTargetFullyReported
fields.title: Is Survey Target Fully Reported
fields.description: A declaration of whether the counts for an instance of the dwc:SurveyTarget report everything that matches the declared dwc:SurveyTarget.
fields.comments: If true (the survey target is fully reported - nothing was left unreported), then this enables inference of absence of detection for everything in that dwc:SurveyTarget that is included but that does not appear in the counts (absent counts signify absence of detection).

fields.name: usagePolicyID
fields.title: Usage Policy ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:UsagePolicy.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: rights
fields.title: Rights
fields.description: Information about rights held in and over the resource. A full-text, readable copyright statement, as required by the national legislation of the copyright holder. On collections, this applies to all contained objects, unless the object itself has a different statement. Examples: “Copyright XY 2008, all rights reserved”, “© 2008 XY Museum” , `Public Domain.`; `Copyright unknown.` Do not place just the name of the copyright holder(s) here! That belongs in a list in the xmpRights:Owner field, which should be supplied if dc:rights is not 'Public Domain', which is appropriate only if the resource is known to be not under copyright. See also the entry for dcterms:rights in this document and see the DCMI FAQ on DC and DCTERMS Namespaces for discussion of the rationale for terms in two namespaces. Normal practice is to use the same Label if both are provided. Labels have no effect on information discovery and are only suggestions.
fields.examples: `Copyright 2014 Ron Thomas` or a URI like `http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/legalcode`
fields.rdfs:comment: Information about rights held in and over the resource. A full-text, readable copyright statement, as required by the national legislation of the copyright holder. On collections, this applies to all contained objects, unless the object itself has a different statement. Examples: “Copyright XY 2008, all rights reserved”, “© 2008 XY Museum” , `Public Domain.`; `Copyright unknown.` Do not place just the name of the copyright holder(s) here! That belongs in a list in the xmpRights:Owner field, which should be supplied if dc:rights is not 'Public Domain', which is appropriate only if the resource is known to be not under copyright. See also the entry for dcterms:rights in this document and see the DCMI FAQ on DC and DCTERMS Namespaces for discussion of the rationale for terms in two namespaces. Normal practice is to use the same Label if both are provided. Labels have no effect on information discovery and are only suggestions.

fields.name: rightsIRI
fields.title: Rights IRI
fields.description: A URI pointing to structured information about rights held in and over the resource. Examples include http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/legalcode and http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. At least one of dcterms:rights and dc:rights must be supplied but, when feasible, supplying both may make the metadata more widely useful. They must specify the same rights. In case of ambiguity, dcterms:rights prevails.
fields.rdfs:comment: A URI pointing to structured information about rights held in and over the resource. Examples include http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/legalcode and http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. At least one of dcterms:rights and dc:rights must be supplied but, when feasible, supplying both may make the metadata more widely useful. They must specify the same rights. In case of ambiguity, dcterms:rights prevails.

fields.name: license
fields.title: License
fields.description: A legal document giving official permission to do something with a resource.
fields.comments: Recommended practice is to identify the license document with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value that identifies the license may be provided.
fields.rdfs:comment: A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource.

fields.name: credit
fields.title: Credit
fields.description: Free text describing how credit should be attributed.
fields.comments: For example, `Please cite this as…`.
fields.rdfs:comment: Free text for `Please cite this as…`
